work.title: The Second Part of King Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

content.text: Enter Gloucester and his Servingmen in mourning cloaks.

lines.text: Thus sometimes hath the brightest day a cloud,
lines.plainText: Thus sometimes hath the brightest day a cloud

lines.text: And after summer evermore succeeds
lines.plainText: And after summer evermore succeeds

lines.text: Barren winter, with his wrathful nipping cold;
lines.plainText: Barren winter with his wrathful nipping cold

lines.text: So cares and joys abound, as seasons fleet.
lines.plainText: So cares and joys abound as seasons fleet

lines.text: Sirs, what's o'clock?
lines.plainText: Sirs what's o'clock

lines.text: Ten, my lord.
lines.plainText: Ten my lord

lines.text: Ten is the hour that was appointed me
lines.plainText: Ten is the hour that was appointed me

lines.text: To watch the coming of my punished duchess.
lines.plainText: To watch the coming of my punished duchess

lines.text: Uneath may she endure the flinty streets,
lines.plainText: Uneath may she endure the flinty streets

lines.text: To tread them with her tender-feeling feet.
lines.plainText: To tread them with her tenderfeeling feet

lines.text: Sweet Nell, ill can thy noble mind abrook
lines.plainText: Sweet Nell ill can thy noble mind abrook

lines.text: The abject people gazing on thy face
lines.plainText: The abject people gazing on thy face

lines.text: With envious looks, laughing at thy shame,
lines.plainText: With envious looks laughing at thy shame

lines.text: That erst did follow thy proud chariot wheels
lines.plainText: That erst did follow thy proud chariot wheels

lines.text: When thou didst ride in triumph through the streets.
lines.plainText: When thou didst ride in triumph through the streets

lines.text: But, soft! I think she comes; and I'll prepare
lines.plainText: But soft I think she comes and I'll prepare

lines.text: My tear-stained eyes to see her miseries.
lines.plainText: My tearstained eyes to see her miseries

content.text: Enter the Duchess of Gloucester in a white sheet, and a taper burning in her hand; with Sir John Stanley, the Sheriff, and Officers.

lines.text: So please your Grace, we'll take her from the sheriff.
lines.plainText: So please your Grace we'll take her from the sheriff

lines.text: No, stir not for your lives; let her pass by.
lines.plainText: No stir not for your lives let her pass by

lines.text: Come you, my lord, to see my open shame?
lines.plainText: Come you my lord to see my open shame

lines.text: Now thou dost penance too. Look how they gaze!
lines.plainText: Now thou dost penance too Look how they gaze

lines.text: See how the giddy multitude do point,
lines.plainText: See how the giddy multitude do point

lines.text: And nod their heads, and throw their eyes on thee.
lines.plainText: And nod their heads and throw their eyes on thee

lines.text: Ah, Gloucester, hide thee from their hateful looks,
lines.plainText: Ah Gloucester hide thee from their hateful looks

lines.text: And, in thy closet pent up, rue my shame,
lines.plainText: And in thy closet pent up rue my shame

lines.text: And ban thine enemies, both mine and thine!
lines.plainText: And ban thine enemies both mine and thine

lines.text: Be patient, gentle Nell, forget this grief.
lines.plainText: Be patient gentle Nell forget this grief

lines.text: Ah, Gloucester, teach me to forget myself!
lines.plainText: Ah Gloucester teach me to forget myself

lines.text: For whilst I think I am thy married wife
lines.plainText: For whilst I think I am thy married wife

lines.text: And thou a prince, Protector of this land,
lines.plainText: And thou a prince Protector of this land

lines.text: Methinks I should not thus be led along,
lines.plainText: Methinks I should not thus be led along

lines.text: Mailed up in shame, with papers on my back,
lines.plainText: Mailed up in shame with papers on my back

lines.text: And followed with a rabble that rejoice
lines.plainText: And followed with a rabble that rejoice

lines.text: To see my tears and hear my deep-fet groans.
lines.plainText: To see my tears and hear my deepfet groans

lines.text: The ruthless flint doth cut my tender feet,
lines.plainText: The ruthless flint doth cut my tender feet

lines.text: And when I start, the envious people laugh
lines.plainText: And when I start the envious people laugh

lines.text: And bid me be advised how I tread.
lines.plainText: And bid me be advised how I tread

lines.text: Ah, Humphrey, can I bear this shameful yoke?
lines.plainText: Ah Humphrey can I bear this shameful yoke

lines.text: Trowest thou that e'er I'll look upon the world,
lines.plainText: Trowest thou that e'er I'll look upon the world

lines.text: Or count them happy that enjoy the sun?
lines.plainText: Or count them happy that enjoy the sun

lines.text: No, dark shall be my light and night my day;
lines.plainText: No dark shall be my light and night my day

lines.text: To think upon my pomp shall be my hell.
lines.plainText: To think upon my pomp shall be my hell

lines.text: Sometimes I'll say, I am Duke Humphrey's wife,
lines.plainText: Sometimes I'll say I am Duke Humphrey's wife

lines.text: And he a prince and ruler of the land;
lines.plainText: And he a prince and ruler of the land

lines.text: Yet so he ruled and such a prince he was
lines.plainText: Yet so he ruled and such a prince he was

lines.text: As he stood by whilst I, his forlorn duchess,
lines.plainText: As he stood by whilst I his forlorn duchess

lines.text: Was made a wonder and a pointing-stock
lines.plainText: Was made a wonder and a pointingstock

lines.text: To every idle rascal follower.
lines.plainText: To every idle rascal follower

lines.text: But be thou mild and blush not at my shame,
lines.plainText: But be thou mild and blush not at my shame

lines.text: Nor stir at nothing till the axe of death
lines.plainText: Nor stir at nothing till the axe of death

lines.text: Hang over thee, as, sure, it shortly will.
lines.plainText: Hang over thee as sure it shortly will

lines.text: For Suffolk, he that can do all in all
lines.plainText: For Suffolk he that can do all in all

lines.text: With her that hateth thee and hates us all,
lines.plainText: With her that hateth thee and hates us all

lines.text: And York and impious Beaufort, that false priest,
lines.plainText: And York and impious Beaufort that false priest

lines.text: Have all limed bushes to betray thy wings;
lines.plainText: Have all limed bushes to betray thy wings

lines.text: And fly thou how thou canst, they'll tangle thee.
lines.plainText: And fly thou how thou canst they'll tangle thee

lines.text: But fear not thou until thy foot be snared,
lines.plainText: But fear not thou until thy foot be snared

lines.text: Nor never seek prevention of thy foes.
lines.plainText: Nor never seek prevention of thy foes

lines.text: Ah, Nell, forbear! Thou aimest all awry.
lines.plainText: Ah Nell forbear Thou aimest all awry

lines.text: I must offend before I be attainted;
lines.plainText: I must offend before I be attainted

lines.text: And had I twenty times so many foes,
lines.plainText: And had I twenty times so many foes

lines.text: And each of them had twenty times their power,
lines.plainText: And each of them had twenty times their power

lines.text: All these could not procure me any scathe
lines.plainText: All these could not procure me any scathe

lines.text: So long as I am loyal, true, and crimeless.
lines.plainText: So long as I am loyal true and crimeless

lines.text: Wouldst have me rescue thee from this reproach?
lines.plainText: Wouldst have me rescue thee from this reproach

lines.text: Why, yet thy scandal were not wiped away,
lines.plainText: Why yet thy scandal were not wiped away

lines.text: But I in danger for the breach of law.
lines.plainText: But I in danger for the breach of law

lines.text: Thy greatest help is quiet, gentle Nell.
lines.plainText: Thy greatest help is quiet gentle Nell

lines.text: I pray thee, sort thy heart to patience;
lines.plainText: I pray thee sort thy heart to patience

lines.text: These few days' wonder will be quickly worn.
lines.plainText: These few days' wonder will be quickly worn

lines.text: I summon your grace to his majesty's parliament,
lines.plainText: I summon your grace to his majesty's parliament

lines.text: Holden at Bury the first of this next month.
lines.plainText: Holden at Bury the first of this next month

lines.text: And my consent ne'er asked herein before?
lines.plainText: And my consent ne'er asked herein before

lines.text: This is close dealing. Well, I will be there.
lines.plainText: This is close dealing Well I will be there

lines.text: An 't please your grace, here my commission stays,
lines.plainText: An 't please your grace here my commission stays

lines.text: And Sir John Stanley is appointed now
lines.plainText: And Sir John Stanley is appointed now

lines.text: To take her with him to the Isle of Man.
lines.plainText: To take her with him to the Isle of Man

lines.text: Must you, Sir John, protect my lady here?
lines.plainText: Must you Sir John protect my lady here

lines.text: So am I given in charge, may 't please your grace.
lines.plainText: So am I given in charge may 't please your grace

lines.text: Entreat her not the worse in that I pray
lines.plainText: Entreat her not the worse in that I pray

lines.text: You use her well. The world may laugh again,
lines.plainText: You use her well The world may laugh again

lines.text: And I may live to do you kindness if
lines.plainText: And I may live to do you kindness if

lines.text: You do it her. And so, Sir John, farewell.
lines.plainText: You do it her And so Sir John farewell

lines.text: What, gone, my lord, and bid me not farewell?
lines.plainText: What gone my lord and bid me not farewell

lines.text: Witness my tears, I cannot stay to speak.
lines.plainText: Witness my tears I cannot stay to speak

lines.text: Art thou gone too? All comfort go with thee,
lines.plainText: Art thou gone too All comfort go with thee

lines.text: For none abides with me; my joy is death;
lines.plainText: For none abides with me my joy is death

lines.text: Death, at whose name I oft have been afeard,
lines.plainText: Death at whose name I oft have been afeard

lines.text: Because I wished this world's eternity.
lines.plainText: Because I wished this world's eternity

lines.text: Stanley, I prithee, go, and take me hence,
lines.plainText: Stanley I prithee go and take me hence

lines.text: I care not whither, for I beg no favour,
lines.plainText: I care not whither for I beg no favour

lines.text: Only convey me where thou art commanded.
lines.plainText: Only convey me where thou art commanded

lines.text: Why, madam, that is to the Isle of Man,
lines.plainText: Why madam that is to the Isle of Man

lines.text: There to be used according to your state.
lines.plainText: There to be used according to your state

lines.text: That's bad enough, for I am but reproach;
lines.plainText: That's bad enough for I am but reproach

lines.text: And shall I then be used reproachfully?
lines.plainText: And shall I then be used reproachfully

lines.text: Like to a duchess, and Duke Humphrey's lady;
lines.plainText: Like to a duchess and Duke Humphrey's lady

lines.text: According to that state you shall be used.
lines.plainText: According to that state you shall be used

lines.text: Sheriff, farewell, and better than I fare,
lines.plainText: Sheriff farewell and better than I fare

lines.text: Although thou hast been conduct of my shame.
lines.plainText: Although thou hast been conduct of my shame

lines.text: It is my office; and, madam, pardon me.
lines.plainText: It is my office and madam pardon me

lines.text: Ay, ay, farewell; thy office is discharged.
lines.plainText: Ay ay farewell thy office is discharged

lines.text: Come, Stanley, shall we go?
lines.plainText: Come Stanley shall we go

lines.text: Madam, your penance done, throw off this sheet,
lines.plainText: Madam your penance done throw off this sheet

lines.text: And go we to attire you for our journey.
lines.plainText: And go we to attire you for our journey

lines.text: My shame will not be shifted with my sheet,
lines.plainText: My shame will not be shifted with my sheet

lines.text: No, it will hang upon my richest robes
lines.plainText: No it will hang upon my richest robes

lines.text: And show itself, attire me how I can.
lines.plainText: And show itself attire me how I can

lines.text: Go, lead the way, I long to see my prison.
lines.plainText: Go lead the way I long to see my prison
